title: Oceanic Anoxic Event 2 (Cenomanian–Turonian)
summary: Oceanic Anoxic Event 2 occurred at the Cenomanian–Turonian boundary, about 93.9 million years ago, and lasted about 500 thousand years in one estimate and 430–445 kyr in another. It was one of the most extreme carbon cycle perturbations in Earth's history; euxinic bottom waters may have covered about 5% of the global seafloor.

uncertainty.note: Start 93.9 Ma and duration about 500 kyr (Owens et al. 2013) give the end at about 93.4 Ma; Voigt et al. 2008 estimate 430-445 kyr from an orbital time scale at Wunstorf.

when.display: c. 93.9 million years ago, lasting 430–500 thousand years

where.modern_name: Wunstorf, Lower Saxony, Germany (global stratigraphic reference section for OAE 2; the event was worldwide)
where.historical_name: Wunstorf section, northern Germany (Cretaceous shelf sea; no polities)

importance.justification: A Cretaceous carbon-cycle and ocean-oxygen crisis recorded in black shales worldwide.

sources.title: Sulfur isotopes track the global extent and dynamics of euxinia during Cretaceous Oceanic Anoxic Event 2 (PNAS 110:18407-18412)
sources.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS)
sources.author: Jeremy D. Owens et al.

sources.title: The Cenomanian-Turonian of the Wunstorf section (North Germany): global stratigraphic reference section and new orbital time scale for Oceanic Anoxic Event 2 (Newsletters on Stratigraphy 43:65-89)
sources.author: Silke Voigt et al.

sources.title: GPlates Web Service reconstruction, MERDITH2021 model

reviewer_note: Least sure of the pin: the event was worldwide and the Wikidata point is the town of Wunstorf, not the exact section. The two durations (about 500 kyr vs 430-445 kyr) differ, so the end date is approximate. Start of 93.9 Ma is from the PNAS article text.
